correctness.rationale: Properness gives the \(\Delta\) lower bound, a C4 forces four colors, and an odd cycle forces three. For the matching upper bound, root the cactus block-cut tree. At an attachment vertex x, a new cycle has two incident edges and at most \(\deg(x)-2\) previously used incident colors, so at least two palette colors remain. A C4 uses those two plus two further distinct colors; any other even cycle alternates the two; an attached odd cycle has K>=3 and can be completed with a third color. Bridges take any unused incident color. Because every cycle of a cactus is wholly contained in one cycle block, no cross-block C4 exists, so the local construction is global. The frozen verifier exhaustively checks all 6074 connected labeled cacti through six vertices using the independent conflict-graph chromatic formulation; that finite census is corroborative, not the infinite proof.

This is a natural family classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation.

final_claim: For every finite connected cactus with at least one edge, \(q_B(G)=\max\{\Delta(G),4\}\) when G contains a 4-cycle, \(q_B(G)=3\) when G itself is an odd cycle, and \(q_B(G)=\Delta(G)\) otherwise; in particular every cactus with \(\Delta\ge4\) is degree-optimal and the threshold four is sharp.
